correctness.rationale: The 2x2 exponential matrices multiply to the exact stated formula. A slow/fast eigenmode decomposition proves convergence of unsplit regularization. The scaled Strang endpoint approaches (cos² theta, cos theta sin theta) uniformly in phase, giving the full circle because theta tends continuously to infinity. Weighted error squared reduces to t²+(1−2t)cos² theta, with attained min/max. Exact energy contractivity follows from skew-adjointness in E_epsilon and positive damping. Exact/symbolic algebra plus 80 numerical checks corroborate all steps; experiments are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The regularization and energy-conserving/dissipative split are standard meaningful modeling and integration choices for descriptor systems. The theorem pinpoints a sharp, uniform-in-phase positive lower error in the natural energy norm at every fixed step despite unconditional contractivity, with a complete circle of endpoint limits and an exact phase-independent half-unit case. This directly diagnoses why fixed-epsilon convergence and geometric stability alone cannot certify an asymptotic-preserving discretization. It does not inflate its claim to other DAEs, subsolvers or coupled limits.
